          Fenerbahçe 3-2 Liverpool Stats: Muriqi Makes His Mark as Kuyt Gets One Over on Former Club
        
      
                          
                      Nov 4, 2026
          
                      Patric Ridge / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Dirk Kuyt enjoyed a Champions League reunion with Liverpool, as his Fenerbahçe team fought back to win 3-2 in Istanbul.
Vedat Muriqi‘s maiden Champions League goal saw Fenerbahçe, who twice came from behind, beat Liverpool 3-2.
Fener went into Wednesday's contest at Sukru Saracoglu Stadium without a win to their name in this season's competition.
Yet against his former club, Fener interim coach Dirk Kuyt masterminded a surprise victory, with substitute Muriqi the hosts' hero with a 79th-minute header.
Liverpool set the tone by having four shots in the opening five minutes, which is the first time they have managed such a feat in a Champions League match since March 2009 (vs Real Madrid).
However, Liverpool were perhaps fortunate not to concede a penalty when Kostas Tsimikas put both hands in the back of Mason Greenwood in the Reds' area.
And Fener were soon behind, with Trey Nyoni volleying in, via a deflection, after meeting a poor clearance on the edge of the hosts' box.
Irfan Can Kahveci prodded Archie Brown's centre against the crossbar from point-blank range as Fener sought an instant response.
But Kuyt's team had their equaliser in the 29th minute, with Greenwood's free-kick taking a big deflection off Jérémy Jacquet and leaving Alisson flat-footed.
Greenwood might have had a second soon after, but Romelu Lukaku's cutback was put behind the former Manchester United forward.
Bradley Barcola drew a sharp stop from Ederson shortly after the restart, while Fener's goalkeeper also had to keep out a Virgil van Dijk header.
Yet a triple Liverpool change paid immediate dividends when, three minutes after coming on, Cody Gakpo crossed in for his fellow substitute Alexander Isak to head home.

Liverpool's lead, once again, lasted just four minutes, however. Alisson got caught in no-man's land from a well-worked corner, with Gakpo only able to flick the ball on for Brown, who had capitalised on Dominik Szoboszlai's sloppiness, to tuck in at the back post.

It marked only the second time ever that two English players have scored against an English team in a Champions League match, after Frank Lampard and Wayne Bridge for Chelsea vs Arsenal in April 2004.

And six minutes later, Fener had swung the tide completely. Three Liverpool players failed to deal with a looping cross, and with Alisson stuck on his line, Muriqi sent a brilliant header into the left-hand corner.
Ederson had to deny Van Dijk once more and Gakpo tried his luck from range, but Liverpool slipped to their first Champions League loss under Andoni Iraola.
Kuyt scored nine goals in 37 Champions League games for Liverpool, and the Dutchman might just have put himself in line to take the Fener job full-time.
They might be giants of Turkish football, but this is Fener's first appearance in the Champions League proper since 2008-09, when they exited in the group stage.
This victory snaps a run of 10 games without a win in the competition, which was their longest winless run in the Champions League.

Indeed, Rio Ngumoha had only just been born when Fener last won a Champions League match. The Liverpool winger became the youngest English player and youngest player for an English club to start each of his side's first four games of a Champions League campaign.
